reason: Start with the after-meal condition to follow how the pancreas responds to absorbed glucose.
expectation: I expect pancreatic beta cells to release insulin, initiating glucose storage or uptake.

alternatives.reason: The between-meal response is also relevant, but I prefer to follow the meal first.

effect: The after-meal signal releases insulin that reaches both muscle and liver, so I can follow either target.
reaction: The separate branches make the next choices clear.
reason: Follow insulin to skeletal muscle to see how it handles glucose after a meal.
expectation: I expect insulin to promote glucose uptake by muscle, possibly with some glucose stored as glycogen.

alternatives.reason: The liver is another insulin target, but I want to follow muscle first.

effect: Insulin increases muscle glucose transport, and its release signal weakens as blood glucose falls; I can now follow the liver branch.
reaction: The membrane transporters make the hormone's distant effect concrete.
reason: Follow insulin to the liver to complete the after-meal response.
expectation: I expect insulin to promote glucose storage as liver glycogen, though the result may show other effects too.

alternatives.reason: The between-meal response matters too, but I want to finish the after-meal branch first.

effect: The liver stores glucose as glycogen and reduces glucose output after a meal, completing that goal. Its depicted glucose entry differs from muscle's.
reaction: The distinction between liver and muscle transport is useful.
reason: Follow the only available combination to investigate the between-meal response.
expectation: I expect lower blood glucose to prompt pancreatic alpha cells to release glucagon, which may signal the liver to release glucose.

effect: Lower glucose is associated with increased glucagon release and decreased insulin release; the highlighted glucagon route leads to the liver.
reaction: The contrast with the after-meal response is clear.
reason: Follow the only available combination to see how the liver maintains blood glucose between meals.
expectation: I expect glucagon to promote liver glycogen breakdown and glucose release into the blood.

effect: Glucagon promotes liver glycogen breakdown and glucose release; its stimulation then decreases as blood glucose rises, completing the between-meal goal.
reaction: The feedback makes the contrast with storage after a meal clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following insulin to muscle and liver was most worthwhile: the picture plans distinguish increased muscle transporter presence from liver glycogen storage, rather than implying identical responses.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial glucagon-release step was clear but predictable, and its panel added little beyond identifying the hormone and its target.

surprise.text: The explicit contrast between liver glucose entry and muscle transporter insertion sharpened my understanding of their different responses to insulin.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the compatible-option menu guided the sequence rather than requiring me to discover the connections.

continue.text: I would continue: comparing the two conditions and their feedback was useful, though the largely predictable, guided sequence offered limited decisions.
